Here’s what you need to read Figma files via the REST API with a Personal Access Token (PAT) as of March 16, 2026:

Required scopes for “read file” use cases
- File JSON or node data: file_content:read (used by GET /v1/files/:key, /v1/files/:key/nodes, and /v1/images/:key). ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/file-endpoints/))
- File metadata only (no document content): file_metadata:read (GET /v1/files/:key/meta). ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/file-endpoints/))
- Read comments (if needed): file_comments:read. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/scopes/))
- Identify the calling user (optional): current_user:read. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/scopes/))
- Note: files:read is now deprecated—use the granular scopes above instead. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/scopes/))

Access and sharing (who can the PAT see?)
- Scopes don’t override sharing/permissions. The PAT can only access files that the PAT owner’s Figma account can access (because they created the file, were invited, or have team/project access). ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/scopes/))
- Granting access: invite the PAT owner’s email to the file/project/team with Can view, or configure link sharing per your org’s policy. Viewer access is sufficient for read-only endpoints. ([help.figma.com](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040531773-Share-files-and-prototypes?utm_source=openai))

Viewer vs. editor and rate limits
- Seat type affects API limits. View/Collab seats can be heavily constrained (e.g., Tier 1 endpoints like GET file can be limited to “up to 6 per month” on Starter plans), while Dev/Full seats get higher per‑minute limits. For automations, ensure the PAT owner has an appropriate seat on the plan that hosts the file. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/rate-limits/?utm_source=openai))

Token creation and usage
- Create a PAT in Settings → Security; choose scopes and an expiration, then send it in the X-Figma-Token header. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/authentication/?utm_source=openai))
- Since April 28, 2025, PATs can have a maximum expiry of 90 days—plan for rotation. Also, “Projects” endpoints now require approval. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/changelog/?utm_source=openai))

Quick checklist
- Give the PAT owner at least “Can view” access to the target file (or appropriate inherited access). ([help.figma.com](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040531773-Share-files-and-prototypes?utm_source=openai))
- Request only the scopes you need (file_content:read and/or file_metadata:read, plus any others your workflow requires). ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/scopes/))
- Consider seat/plan rate limits for your use case. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/rate-limits/?utm_source=openai))

If you tell me exactly what you want to read (full document JSON, specific nodes, images, comments, or just metadata), I can list the minimal scopes and example requests for that flow. ([developers.figma.com](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/file-endpoints/))

I can help you **read and analyze Figma content**, but I can’t personally “log into Figma like a human” from here unless you give this workspace a machine-readable way to access it.

## Best ways to do it

### Option 1: Safest and simplest
Export the important material from Figma into this workspace.

Good exports:
- PDF exports of key flows
- PNG screenshots of important frames
- copied text from strategy, product, sales, or design pages
- FigJam exports
- component library docs
- board screenshots with annotations

Put them in:
- `inbox/figma/`

Then I can:
- read them
- summarize what Raidyn is, how the product works, key user flows, design language, open questions
- update the right company and work-item records

This is the **lowest-risk** option.

---

### Option 2: Read-only Figma API access
If you want me to inspect Figma more directly, you can give this workspace a **read-only Figma API token**.

## What you would need
Create a Figma personal access token with the smallest useful scopes:

- `file_content:read`
- `file_metadata:read`

Optional if you want deeper context:
- `file_comments:read`
- `file_versions:read`

Also:
- the Figma account that owns the token must already have access to the files
- viewer access is enough for read-only use

## Important security note
Do **not** paste a token into chat if you want to avoid it being stored in conversation history.

Better:
- store it in a local non-committed env file like `.env.local`
- or in a local shell session environment variable
- and give me the file links or file keys

## Then I can help by
- fetching file metadata
- reading file structure and page names
- extracting frames/nodes/images
- identifying product flows, screens, terminology, personas, and design-system clues
- turning that into clean internal records for Raidyn

---

## What I cannot promise
Even with full read-only Figma access, I still won’t “know everything” about Raidyn.

Figma is great for:
- product flows
- UX decisions
- messaging
- internal boards
- roadmaps
- sales or investor decks if they live there

But it won’t fully replace:
- internal docs
- CRM/pipeline context
- customer conversations
- roadmap decisions
- company strategy notes

So Figma is **very useful**, but not the whole picture.

---

## My recommendation
Use this order:

1. Give me the **top 3–10 most important Figma files**
2. Start with either:

3. I produce:
   - a Raidyn context brief

   - a list of gaps and assumptions
   - updates to `entities/companies/co-raidyn/record.md`

---

1. Create a read-only Figma token
2. Save it in `.env.local`:

3. Give me the Figma file links you want analyzed

Then I can help with the rest.
